newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour to weigh British interests on EMU - Brown.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour to weigh British interests on EMU - Brown.

text.p: Gordon Brown, economics spokesman of the opposition Labour Party, on Monday denied party policy on the European single currency has changed, and said it would take the decision after weighing the national economic interest.

"We are not like the Liberals who would go in anyway, we are not like the Conservatives who are divided over the issue...we will make the decision on the national economic interest," Brown told BBC radio.

On Sunday, Labour foreign affairs spokesman Robin Cook made what Conservatives claimed was a u-turn on the single currency by declaring that if a Labour government did not take Britain in in 1999, it would be unlikely to do so in the course of the next parliament.

Brown defended Cook's remarks. He said Cook had been saying that if monetary union was postponed in 1999, it would be unlikely to go ahead in the years immediately following. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5425528
